study_type.note: Quasi-experimental staggered DiD on mined GitHub data; Quasi-experiment would also fit, but both extractors lead with Repository mining.

research_method.claude: Repository mining, quasi-experimental: staggered DiD (Borusyak et al. imputation estimator), propensity score matching (1:3), dynamic panel GMM (Arellano-Bond); robustness checks (TWFE, Callaway & Sant'Anna); 806 treated + 1,380 control repositories, monthly Jan 2024–Aug 2025
research_method.nlm: Repository mining, quantitative: staggered DiD with propensity score matching and dynamic panel GMM; robustness analyses; 806 Cursor-adopting and 1,380 matched control repositories, Jan 2024–Aug 2025
research_method.value: Repository mining with a quasi-experimental staggered difference-in-differences design (Borusyak et al. estimator) on propensity-score-matched controls, plus dynamic panel GMM models (Arellano-Bond); SonarQube-based quality metrics; robustness checks on sustained-use and active-repository subsets; 806 Cursor-adopting vs 1,380 matched control repositories, monthly panel
research_method.note: Estimator names and 1:3 matching ratio stated only by Claude (not contradicted).

evidence.quote: We then use a difference-in-differences (DiD) design with staggered adoption [28, 30], comparing repositories that adopt Cursor at different times to a matched control group that never adopts during our observation period.
we use propensity score matching [25] to select 1,380 similar repositories from those never adopting Cursor during our observation period.
we fit dynamic panel generalized method of moments (GMM) models [22] to support our interpretation of the DiD results
we follow prior work [58, 61, 102] by requiring at least 10 stars at collection time
For each repository in the treatment and control group, we collect monthly outcome metrics and time-varying covariates from January 2024 to August 2025.
This yields 806 repositories with adoption dates between January 2024 and March 2025 that are still available on GitHub at the time of data analysis (August 2025).
In this paper, we estimate the causal effect of adopting a widely popular LLM agent assistant, namely Cursor, on development velocity and software quality.
Commitsit : Number of commits in repository i at month t; • Lines Addedit : Total lines added, summed over all commits in repository i at month t. Both have been used as productivity proxies
Static Analysis Warningsit : Total number of reliability, maintainability, and security issues for repository i at month t, as detected by SonarQube's static analysis.
Static analysis warnings increase by 30% and code complexity increases by 41% post-adoption according to the Borusyak et al. [28] DiD estimator.
